body: Beall, Jc, Restall, Greg, Sagi, Gil, in the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry "Logical Consequence" says: "A good argument is one whose conclusions follow from its premises; its conclusions are consequences of, or entailed by , its premises. But in what sense do conclusions follow from premises? What is it for a conclusion to be a consequence of , or entailed by , premises? Those questions, in many respects, are at the heart of logic (as a philosophical discipline). In this entry we'll primarily talk in terms of conclusions following from or being a consequence of premises, since entailment is sometimes used elsewhere in philosophy and logic in a different or stronger sense." This card reports that entry's preamble. It does not treat the entry as the original paper it cites.
